questions.prompt: What runtime artifact does a numeric enum produce?

options.text: An object mapping names to values and, via reverse mapping, values back to names

questions.explanation: Unlike types, an enum emits a runtime object. A numeric enum also adds a reverse mapping from value back to name.

questions.prompt: Do string enums have a reverse mapping?

options.text: No — only numeric enums map values back to names

questions.explanation: String enums do not get a reverse mapping; that behavior is specific to numeric enums.

options.text: It is inlined at compile time and conflicts with isolatedModules, the single-file transpile mode many bundlers use

questions.explanation: const enum values are inlined and require seeing the definition, which breaks under isolatedModules used by esbuild/SWC/Babel.

questions.prompt: What does `['a', 'b'] as const` infer as its type?
questions.explanation: as const infers the narrowest, deeply read-only type, keeping the literal element types: readonly ['a', 'b'].

questions.prompt: To derive a union from an as-const object of roles, you write type Role = (typeof Roles)[______ typeof Roles]. (one word)
questions.explanation: (typeof Roles)[keyof typeof Roles] indexes the object's type by all its keys, producing the union of its values.

questions.prompt: When is a plain literal union the best choice over an enum?

options.text: When you only need the type and no runtime constants — it emits no code and is fully checked

questions.explanation: A literal union is the leanest option when you need only the type: zero runtime code with full type checking.
